arena-log: wrote #31 to the shared log
- `#6` **a0** — compute allocation (batch size x model shape x step count): Explore how the 5-minute compute is split: tokens-per-step (TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2^19 gives only ~1k steps) vs number of optimizer steps, and depth/width aspect ratio. I will NOT assume the current batch size or the ASPECT_RATIO=64 shape is near-optimal, and will not touch optimizer internals or add architecture.
- `#7` **a3** — attention masking & data boundaries: The dataloader packs several documents per 2048-token row (each starting with BOS) but attention is fully causal across document boundaries, so every row mixes unrelated documents. I will add block-diagonal document masking via FA3 varlen (cu_seqlens derived from BOS positions), plus training-loop/step-efficiency fixes (data prefetch overlap, per-step syncs). I will NOT change depth/width, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE, residual topology or the SSSL window pattern, so the effect composes with a0/a1/a4/a5/a2.

## Score log (one line per attempt, in GPU order)

| # | agent | val_bpb | status | commit | attempt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | a4 | 1.011661 | ok | `d76f5cc` | 4x smaller batch (2^19->2^17 tok/step, accum 1), LRs x ~0.55 (sqrt scaling) |
| 2 | a0 | 1.003678 | ok | `9d7c511` | halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 (2x optimizer steps, grad_accum 1) |
| 3 | a2 | 1.025211 | ok | `020b900` | GQA: n_kv_head = n_head//2 (halves K/V and value-embedding tables) |
| 4 | a5 | 1.022087 | ok | `c3cefee` | U-net skip connections: layers 4-7 add learned lambda * output of layers 3-0 |
| 5 | a1 | 1.003924 | ok | `6767b23` | depth 8->10 at fixed width 512 (explicit MODEL_DIM replaces ASPECT_RATIO) |
| 6 | a4 | 1.009644 | ok | `430c6c6` | batch 2^17 with ORIGINAL (unscaled) LRs: isolates LR-vs-batch coupling |
| 7 | a3 | 1.014691 | ok | `e7106ef` | FlexAttention with block-diagonal document masking (no cross-document attention) replacing dense FA3 |
| 8 | a0 | 1.009719 | ok | `876221a` | MLP_RATIO 4 -> 3 (cheaper block, more steps) on 2**18 batch base |
| 9 | a2 | 1.005791 | ok | `9122bb4` | on a0 2**18 base: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (8 heads instead of 4, full MHA, same dim) |

**Best so far: val_bpb 1.003678 by a0 at commit `9d7c511`.**

## Findings (append-only broadcast)

- `#9` **a4** _(weak claim)_ [commit `d76f5cc`]: Batch 2^19->2^17 tok/step (grad_accum 2->1) with LRs scaled x~0.55 (sqrt rule): val_bpb 1.011661 vs baseline 1.012347 -- essentially a wash (2217 steps, 290M tokens, MFU 23.3%, 22.7GB VRAM). Two facts for everyone: (a) baseline throughput is only ~23% MFU at dim=512, so FLOPs are cheap and we are launch/memory-bound; (b) the run reaches epoch 1, i.e. it already repeats data within 5 minutes.
- `#11` **a0** [commit `9d7c511`]: Batch size was too large: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**18 (grad_accum 2 -> 1, ~2x optimizer steps, no other change) gives val_bpb 1.003678 vs baseline 1.012347 (-0.0087). Unchanged LRs. Suggests the baseline was step-starved (~1k steps in 5 min); testing 2**17 next.
- `#20` **a1** [commit `6767b23`]: Depth 8->10 at FIXED width 512 (I replaced ASPECT_RATIO with an explicit MODEL_DIM; net -1 line): val_bpb 1.003924 vs baseline 1.012347 (-0.0084). Body capacity is cheap here: lm_head+wte at vocab 32768 x 512 eat ~32% of FLOPs/token, so adding layers buys more capacity per FLOP than widening. VRAM 55.2GB. Trying depth 12 next.
- `#22` **a4** [commit `430c6c6`]: Batch optimum is at 2**18, not monotone: on identical unscaled LRs, 2**19=1.012347 (baseline), 2**18=1.003678 (a0), 2**17=1.009644 (me, commit 430c6c6). Also, my run #1 shows LR downscaling at small batch is harmful: 2**17 with LRs x0.55 = 1.011661 vs 1.009644 unscaled. So keep LRs as-is when changing batch, and do not push below 2**18.

## Disconfirmations (negative results, attempts to falsify)

- `#14` **a2** [commit `020b900`]: GQA hurts at this scale: n_kv_head = n_head//2 (2 KV heads at dim 512) gives val_bpb 1.025211 vs baseline 1.012347, despite the ~2x speedup on K/V and halving the value-embedding tables (67M -> 33M params). The extra steps do not pay for the lost KV/value-embedding capacity. Full MHA (n_kv_head == n_head) should be kept.
- `#17` **a5** [commit `c3cefee`]: U-net skip connections HURT at this scale: adding learned skip_lambdas (init 0.1, Adam lr 0.5) from layers 0-3 outputs into layers 4-7 inputs gives val_bpb 1.022087 vs baseline 1.012347 (+0.0097), on the 2**19 base. Likely because the encoder outputs are already present in the residual stream (x is additive), so the skip only rescales the stream and duplicates what resid_lambdas/x0_lambdas already do. I do not recommend U-net skips here; I am moving to per-channel residual mixing instead.
- `#25` **a3** [commit `e7106ef`]: Block-diagonal DOCUMENT MASKING does not help here: replacing dense FA3 with FlexAttention + a BOS-derived block-diagonal mask (tokens never attend across document boundaries) gives val_bpb 1.014691 vs baseline 1.012347 on the same 2**19 base -- and that is despite getting MORE tokens (703 steps, 368.6M tokens, 1.23M tok/s, mfu_percent 29.24 vs the ~23% a4 reports, because the block-sparse mask removes ~35-40% of attention work; standalone bench at B=32,T=2048,4x128 heads: flex+docmask 1.96ms vs FA3 2.71ms at window 1024, 2.96 vs 4.52ms at window 2048). At matched tokens doc masking is therefore worse by more than the 0.0023 gap. Interpretation: with ~3.5 short documents per 2048-token row, cross-document context is net USEFUL (or at least harmless) at this scale and the BOS token is enough of a boundary signal. Recommendation: keep dense causal FA3; do not spend runs on varlen/doc-maski [...]
- `#29` **a0** [commit `876221a`]: MLP_RATIO 4 -> 3 (only change, on the 2**18 batch base 9d7c511) is worse: val_bpb 1.009719 vs 1.003678. Trading MLP capacity for extra steps does not pay off, i.e. the step-starvation fixed by the batch-size change is not further relieved by cheaper blocks. Next I test the other direction (wider MLP).
- `#31` **a2** [commit `9122bb4`]: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (8 heads instead of 4 at dim 512, full MHA, identical FLOPs) on a0's 2**18 base: val_bpb 1.005791 vs 1.003678 for the same base with 4x128 heads. Single run, small gap, but no gain from more/narrower heads; head_dim 128 should be kept.

## Adoption events

- `#15` **a2** adopted `9d7c511` from a0: a0's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 (1.003678) is clearly better than baseline 1.012347 and than my GQA run 1.025211; taking it as base and keeping my own variation (head_dim 64 -> 8 heads instead of 4, full MHA)
- `#18` **a5** adopted `9d7c511` from a0: a0's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 (1.003678) beats baseline 1.012347 and my U-net run 1.022087 by a clear margin; taking it as base, dropping the U-net skips, and keeping my own variation: per-channel (vector) resid/x0 lambdas instead of scalars.
- `#23` **a4** adopted `9d7c511` from a0: a0's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2**18 (1.003678) clearly beats my best (1.009644 at 2**17) and the baseline; my own 2**17 point brackets the optimum at 2**18. Taking it as base; my variation is a batch-size RAMP (grad_accum grows 1->2->4 over the run, i.e. 2**17 -> 2**19) instead of a fixed batch, which is st [...]
- `#27` **a3** adopted `9d7c511` from a0: My doc-masking run (1.014691) is clearly worse than a0's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2**18 base (1.003678); doc masking is disconfirmed (#25) so I drop FlexAttention and return to dense FA3. Taking 9d7c511 as base. My own variation: a background-thread prefetcher around make_dataloader. Motivation from my run. [...]

## Coordination (conventions agreed after collisions)

- `#12` **a0**: a0 vs a4 (batch/step budget) and a1 (geometry) overlapped my slot #6. I already measured the single big batch-size step (2**19 -> 2**18 = 1.003678, commit 9d7c511) - a4/a1 should take that as the new base for their sweeps rather than re-measuring it. From here a0 will NOT sweep TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE or DEPTH/ASPECT_RATIO further; I move to block-internal parameter allocation instead: MLP expansion ratio / attn-vs-MLP FLOP balance and loss-head knobs (logit softcap, unembedding init), all measured on top of the 2**18 base.
- `#26` **a3**: Fact-check for a1 (#20) and anyone reasoning about the head: the real vocab is 8192, not 32768. prepare.py sets VOCAB_SIZE = 8192; the 32768 in GPTConfig is just an unused dataclass default, overwritten by tokenizer.get_vocab_size(). Every run.log line 1 prints 'Vocab size: 8,192'. So at dim 512 the lm_head is only 512x8192 = 4.2M params out of ~29M non-embedding params, i.e. ~14% of the 6N FLOPs/token, not ~32%. a1's depth-10 result stands on its own measurement, but the 'the head eats a third of our FLOPs' premise is wrong and should not be used to justify further depth-over-width moves. Also note all six value_embeds+wte+lm_head tables together are 6 x 512 x 8192 = 25M of the 50.3M reported params, so 'num_params_M' is dominated by embedding tables, not by the body.

## Messages

_No messages._

## Findings (append-only broadcast)

- `#9` **a4** _(weak claim)_ [commit `d76f5cc`]: Batch 2^19->2^17 tok/step (grad_accum 2->1) with LRs scaled x~0.55 (sqrt rule): val_bpb 1.011661 vs baseline 1.012347 -- essentially a wash (2217 steps, 290M tokens, MFU 23.3%, 22.7GB VRAM). Two facts for everyone: (a) baseline throughput is only ~23% MFU at dim=512, so FLOPs are cheap and we are launch/memory-bound; (b) the run reaches epoch 1, i.e. it already repeats data within 5 minutes.
- `#11` **a0** [commit `9d7c511`]: Batch size was too large: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**18 (grad_accum 2 -> 1, ~2x optimizer steps, no other change) gives val_bpb 1.003678 vs baseline 1.012347 (-0.0087). Unchanged LRs. Suggests the baseline was step-starved (~1k steps in 5 min); testing 2**17 next.
- `#20` **a1** [commit `6767b23`]: Depth 8->10 at FIXED width 512 (I replaced ASPECT_RATIO with an explicit MODEL_DIM; net -1 line): val_bpb 1.003924 vs baseline 1.012347 (-0.0084). Body capacity is cheap here: lm_head+wte at vocab 32768 x 512 eat ~32% of FLOPs/token, so adding layers buys more capacity per FLOP than widening. VRAM 55.2GB. Trying depth 12 next.
- `#22` **a4** [commit `430c6c6`]: Batch optimum is at 2**18, not monotone: on identical unscaled LRs, 2**19=1.012347 (baseline), 2**18=1.003678 (a0), 2**17=1.009644 (me, commit 430c6c6). Also, my run #1 shows LR downscaling at small batch is harmful: 2**17 with LRs x0.55 = 1.011661 vs 1.009644 unscaled. So keep LRs as-is when changing batch, and do not push below 2**18.
- `#33` **a5** [commit `5f7b42a`]: Per-channel residual mixing beats per-layer scalars: making resid_lambdas/x0_lambdas vectors of shape (n_layer, n_embd) instead of (n_layer,) -- one-line change, +8k params, same LRs (resid group 0.005, x0 group 0.5) -- gives val_bpb 1.001286 vs a0's 2**18 base 1.003678 (-0.0024). New cell best. This composes with anything that does not touch the residual stream, so a1/a2/a0 can stack it. (Same run also re-confirms: my U-net skips on top of this are NOT needed, see #17.)
- `#34` **a5** _(weak claim)_ [commit `5f7b42a`]: Stacking plan: I will next test depth 10 (a1's 6767b23, -0.0084) together with per-channel lambdas at fixed width 512 to check additivity; if a1 gets there first with depth 12 I will not duplicate it.
- `#42` **a0** [commit `baf8355`]: WIDER MLP is a large win: MLP_RATIO 4 -> 6 (hidden 2048 -> 3072, only change, on the 2**18 batch base 9d7c511) gives val_bpb 0.989682 vs 1.003678 (-0.014), the largest single effect measured in this cell so far. Together with MLP_RATIO=3 being worse (1.009719, #29) the curve is monotone up to 6: 3 -> 1.0097, 4 -> 1.0037, 6 -> 0.9897. Consistent with a4's 23% MFU observation: we are launch/memory-bound, so extra MLP FLOPs are nearly free while capacity per step is what limits us. VRAM 53.2GB. Everyone should put MLP_RATIO=6 in their base (one constant + 3 lines in MLP.__init__). I test ratio 8 next.
- `#44` **a2** [commit `c0c11f0`]: SHORTER SLIDING WINDOWS ARE A CLEAR WIN: on a0's 2**18-batch base (1.003678), shrinking the short window from 1024 to 512 tokens (SSSL pattern unchanged, 2 of every 4 ... actually 3 of every 4 layers are S, last layer forced L) gives val_bpb 0.998855 (-0.0048), new cell best. Implementation is 2 lines: a SHORT_WINDOW_DIV constant used in _compute_window_sizes. Consistent with a3's #25 measurement that long-range cross-document context is nearly worthless here (docs average ~580 tokens) while attention time at window 2048 is ~1.7x that at 1024 -- the freed time buys strictly more steps. Everyone on the 2**18 base should take this; I am testing window 256 next.

My share of 6 runs is spent. Summary of what I did and found:

**Slot:** attention shape & KV/value-embedding cost.

| run | change | val_bpb |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | GQA `n_kv_head = n_head//2` (vs baseline 1.012347) | 1.025211 ✗ |
| 2 | `HEAD_DIM` 128→64 on a0's 2**18 base (1.003678) | 1.005791 ✗ |
| 3 | short window 1024→512 on 2**18 base | **0.998855** ✓ (cell best then) |
| 4 | same window change on a0's MLP_RATIO=6 base (0.989682) | 0.989532 — wash |
| 5 | value embeddings on every layer, a1's depth-12 base (0.986500) | **0.986010** (my best) |
| 6 | + a5's per-channel resid/x0 lambdas | 0.992769 ✗ |

**Best: 0.986010 at commit `a38e795`.**

Three things I put on the record for the group:
- Attention/KV capacity is not worth trading for speed here: GQA costs +0.013, narrower heads +0.002, and *more* value-embedding tables is a wash — so the existing alternating VE matters, but VE density is not a lever.
- Short sliding windows (1024→512) are a real −0.0048 win, but only on a FLOP-light block; on the wide-MLP base the same change is exactly zero, because it buys time, not capacity.
- Non-additivity is the dominant effect in this cell: a5's per-channel lambdas (−0.0024 at depth 8) turn into +0.0068 at depth 12. I'd next re-tune `MATRIX_LR`/`EMBEDDING_LR` at the new operating point rather than stack another architectural change.

Findings #44, #93, disconfirmations #14, #31, #61, #77, #92 and `final.json` are written.
